=== e2e.yml ===
name: End-to-End Install Tests

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Published version to test (defaults to latest)"
        required: false
        default: "latest"

env:
  # Keep CI runs out of the usage telemetry.
  FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY: "off"
  FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT: ${{ github.event.inputs.version || 'latest' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  install-e2e:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    name: e2e (${{ matrix.os }}, node ${{ matrix.node }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: 22
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: 24
          - os: macos-15
            node: 24
          - os: windows-latest
            node: 24
          - os: windows-latest
            node: 26
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: 26
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      HAS_OPENAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY != '' }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

      - name: Install published package globally
        # Issue #177 regression: this must succeed on every supported Node,
        # including the newest major — a failing preinstall used to roll the
        # install back and pin users to the previous version.
        run: npm install -g "@companion-ai/feynman@${FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT}"

      - name: feynman --version
        run: |
          set -x
          feynman --version
          installed="$(feynman --version | tail -1)"
          expected="$(npm view "@companion-ai/feynman@${FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT}" version | tail -1)"
          if [ "$installed" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "version mismatch: installed=$installed expected=$expected" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: feynman packages list / update / search status
        run: |
          feynman packages list
          feynman update
          feynman search status

      - name: Pi RPC compatibility check
        run: node "$(npm root -g)/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"

      - name: Configure model auth for live smokes
        if: env.HAS_OPENAI_KEY == 'true'
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          export FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home"
          mkdir -p "$FEYNMAN_HOME/.feynman/agent"
          node -e '
            const { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } = require("node:fs");
            const { join } = require("node:path");
            const home = join(process.env.RUNNER_TEMP, "feynman-home", ".feynman", "agent");
            mkdirSync(home, { recursive: true });
            writeFileSync(join(home, "auth.json"), JSON.stringify({ openai: { type: "api_key", key: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY } }));
            writeFileSync(join(home, "settings.json"), JSON.stringify({ defaultProvider: "openai", defaultModel: "gpt-4.1-mini", quietStartup: true }));
          '
          echo "FEYNMAN_HOME=$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Live model smoke (one-shot prompt)
        if: env.FEYNMAN_HOME != ''
        run: |
          feynman --mode json --prompt 'Reply with exactly CI_OK and nothing else. Do not call any tools.' > smoke.log 2>&1 || { tail -50 smoke.log; exit 1; }
          grep -q "CI_OK" smoke.log
          echo "model smoke ok"

      - name: Live model smoke (text mode)
        if: env.FEYNMAN_HOME != ''
        run: |
          feynman --prompt 'Reply with exactly CI_TEXT_OK and nothing else. Do not call any tools.' > smoke-text.log 2>&1 || { tail -50 smoke-text.log; exit 1; }
          grep -q "CI_TEXT_OK" smoke-text.log
          echo "text mode smoke ok"

      - name: Live native-session subagent smoke
        if: env.FEYNMAN_HOME != ''
        run: |
          feynman --mode json --prompt 'Use the subagent tool to run the "researcher" agent with the task: Reply with the single word PONG and stop. After the subagent returns, reply with exactly RESULT=<the single word the subagent returned> and nothing else.' > subagent.log 2>&1 || { tail -80 subagent.log; exit 1; }
          for marker in "Cannot find module" "is not defined" "requested unavailable child tools"; do
            if grep -q "$marker" subagent.log; then
              echo "subagent regression detected (matched: $marker):" >&2
              grep -n "$marker" subagent.log | head -3 >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          # RESULT=PONG can only appear if the child actually ran and returned
          # its reply; a failed tool call makes the parent relay an error word.
          grep -q "RESULT=PONG" subagent.log || { echo "child output not relayed:" >&2; grep -o "RESULT=[A-Za-z_]*" subagent.log >&2; tail -30 subagent.log >&2; exit 1; }
          grep -o "RESULT=PONG" subagent.log | head -1
          echo "subagent smoke ok"

  published-native-installer-e2e:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    name: native installer (${{ matrix.os }})
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os:
          - ubuntu-latest
          - macos-15
          - windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24.21.0"

      - name: Install the published native bundle through the live Unix installer
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          expected=$(npm view "@companion-ai/feynman@${FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT}" version | tail -1)
          install_root="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-native-install"
          installer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-install.sh"
          curl --fail --location --silent --show-error \
            https://feynman.is/install \
            --output "$installer"
          FEYNMAN_INSTALL_BIN_DIR="$install_root/bin" \
            FEYNMAN_INSTALL_APP_DIR="$install_root/app" \
            FEYNMAN_INSTALL_SKIP_PATH_UPDATE=1 \
            sh "$installer" "$FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT"

          bin="$install_root/bin/feynman"
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$expected"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          case "$(uname -s)" in
            Darwin) os=darwin ;;
            Linux) os=linux ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$(uname -m)" in
            x86_64 | amd64) arch=x64 ;;
            arm64 | aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          bundle="$install_root/app/feynman-$expected-$os-$arch"
          test -x "$bundle/feynman"
          "$bundle/node/bin/node" "$bundle/app/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"

      - name: Install the published native bundle through the live Windows installer
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $expected = (
            & npm view "@companion-ai/feynman@$env:FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT" version |
              Select-Object -Last 1
          ).ToString().Trim()
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Could not resolve the requested npm version."
          }

          $env:LOCALAPPDATA = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "FeynmanLocalAppData"
          $env:FEYNMAN_HOME = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "FeynmanHome"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA -Force | Out-Null
          & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1))) `
            -Version $env:FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT

          $installRoot = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\feynman"
          $bin = Join-Path $installRoot "bin\feynman.cmd"
          $installed = (& $bin --version | Select-Object -Last 1).ToString().Trim()
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $installed -ne $expected) {
            throw "Installed version mismatch: expected=$expected actual=$installed"
          }
          & $bin --help | Out-Null
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Installed Windows launcher failed --help."
          }
          $bundle = Join-Path $installRoot "feynman-$expected-win32-x64"
          & (Join-Path $bundle "node\node.exe") `
            (Join-Path $bundle "app\scripts\check-pi-rpc.mjs")
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Installed Windows bundle failed the Pi RPC compatibility check."
          }

  release-candidate-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    name: Release candidate (PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc

      - name: Validate source and website
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          npm ci
          npm test
          npm run typecheck
          npm run build
          npm run architecture:check
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs
          (
            cd website
            npm ci
            npm run lint
            npm run typecheck
            npm run build
            npm audit --omit=dev
          )
          git diff --check

      - name: Validate packed consumer and runtime
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          npm pack --dry-run --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack-dry-run.json"
          npm pack --json --pack-destination "$RUNNER_TEMP" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack.json"
          tarball="$RUNNER_TEMP/companion-ai-feynman-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").tgz"
          test -s "$tarball"
          node scripts/verify-package-budget.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack.json" "$tarball"

          consumer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-consumer"
          mkdir -p "$consumer"
          (cd "$consumer" && npm init -y >/dev/null)
          npm install --prefix "$consumer" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs --prefix "$consumer"

          bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman"
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" packages list
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" search status
          node "$consumer/node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: pr-npm-package
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-ai-feynman-*.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error

  supported-node-consumers-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: release-candidate-pr
    name: Candidate consumer (${{ matrix.os }}, Node ${{ matrix.node }})
    timeout-minutes: 90
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "22.22.0"
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "26"
          - os: macos-15
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: windows-latest
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: windows-latest
            node: "26"
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Only the audit script; these jobs test the packed tarball, not the source tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: scripts/npm-audit.mjs
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: pr-npm-package
          path: npm-package
      - name: Verify the exact candidate tarball
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          count=$(find npm-package -type f -name '*.tgz' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          test "$count" = "1"
          tarball=$(find npm-package -type f -name '*.tgz' -print)
          tarball=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("node:path").resolve(process.argv[1]))' "$tarball")
          tarball_for_tar="$tarball"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            tarball_for_tar=$(cygpath -u "$tarball")
          fi
          version=$(tar -xOf "$tarball_for_tar" package/package.json | node -e \
            'let source=""; process.stdin.on("data", chunk => source += chunk).on("end", () => process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(source).version))')
          consumer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-consumer"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            consumer=$(cygpath -u "$consumer")
          fi
          mkdir -p "$consumer"
          (cd "$consumer" && npm init -y >/dev/null)
          npm install --prefix "$consumer" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs --prefix "$consumer"
          bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman.cmd"
          fi
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$version"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" packages list
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" search status
          global_prefix="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-global"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            global_prefix=$(cygpath -u "$global_prefix")
            global_bin="$global_prefix/feynman.cmd"
          else
            global_bin="$global_prefix/bin/feynman"
          fi
          npm install --global --prefix "$global_prefix" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          test "$("$global_bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$version"
          "$global_bin" --help >/dev/null
          node "$consumer/node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"
          global_node_modules=$(npm root --global --prefix "$global_prefix")
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            global_node_modules=$(cygpath -u "$global_node_modules")
          fi
          node "$global_node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"

  windows-native-installer-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    name: Windows native installer (PR)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc

      - name: Build Windows native ZIP
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          npm ci --ignore-scripts
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "npm ci failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }

          npm run build
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "npm run build failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }

          npm run build:native-bundle
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "npm run build:native-bundle failed: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $archive)) {
            throw "Expected native archive was not produced: $archive"
          }
          if ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $archive).Length -eq 0) {
            throw "Native archive is empty: $archive"
          }
          Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
          $smokeRoot = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP ("feynman-native-rpc-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N"))
          [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::ExtractToDirectory($archive, $smokeRoot)
          $bundleRoot = Join-Path $smokeRoot "feynman-$version-win32-x64"
          $native = Join-Path $bundleRoot "feynman.cmd"
          $nativeNode = Join-Path $bundleRoot "node/node.exe"
          & $native --help | Select-Object -First 20
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Windows native launcher failed --help: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }
          & $nativeNode (Join-Path $bundleRoot "app/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs")
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Windows native bundle failed the Pi RPC compatibility check: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }

      - name: Install candidate with Windows PowerShell 5.1
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          & ./scripts/verify-windows-installer.ps1 `
            -ArchivePath $archive `
            -Version $version

      - name: Install candidate with PowerShell Core
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          & ./scripts/verify-windows-installer.ps1 `
            -ArchivePath $archive `
            -Version $version

          feynman --prompt 'Reply with exactly CI_TEXT_OK and nothing else. Do not call any tools.' > smoke-text.log 2>&1 || { tail -50 smoke-text.log; exit 1; }
          grep -q "CI_TEXT_OK" smoke-text.log
          echo "text mode smoke ok"

      - name: Live native-session subagent smoke
        if: env.FEYNMAN_HOME != ''
        run: |
          feynman --mode json --prompt 'Use the subagent tool to run the "researcher" agent with the task: Reply with the single word PONG and stop. After the subagent returns, reply with exactly RESULT=<the single word the subagent returned> and nothing else.' > subagent.log 2>&1 || { tail -80 subagent.log; exit 1; }
          for marker in "Cannot find module" "is not defined" "requested unavailable child tools"; do
            if grep -q "$marker" subagent.log; then
              echo "subagent regression detected (matched: $marker):" >&2
              grep -n "$marker" subagent.log | head -3 >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          # RESULT=PONG can only appear if the child actually ran and returned
          # its reply; a failed tool call makes the parent relay an error word.
          grep -q "RESULT=PONG" subagent.log || { echo "child output not relayed:" >&2; grep -o "RESULT=[A-Za-z_]*" subagent.log >&2; tail -30 subagent.log >&2; exit 1; }
          grep -o "RESULT=PONG" subagent.log | head -1
          echo "subagent smoke ok"

  published-native-installer-e2e:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    name: native installer (${{ matrix.os }})
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os:
          - ubuntu-latest
          - macos-15
          - windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24.21.0"

      - name: Install the published native bundle through the live Unix installer
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          expected=$(npm view "@companion-ai/feynman@${FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT}" version | tail -1)
          install_root="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-native-install"
          installer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-install.sh"
          curl --fail --location --silent --show-error \
            https://feynman.is/install \
            --output "$installer"
          FEYNMAN_INSTALL_BIN_DIR="$install_root/bin" \
            FEYNMAN_INSTALL_APP_DIR="$install_root/app" \
            FEYNMAN_INSTALL_SKIP_PATH_UPDATE=1 \
            sh "$installer" "$FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT"

          bin="$install_root/bin/feynman"
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$expected"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          case "$(uname -s)" in
            Darwin) os=darwin ;;
            Linux) os=linux ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$(uname -m)" in
            x86_64 | amd64) arch=x64 ;;
            arm64 | aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
            *) exit 1 ;;
          esac
          bundle="$install_root/app/feynman-$expected-$os-$arch"
          test -x "$bundle/feynman"
          "$bundle/node/bin/node" "$bundle/app/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"

      - name: Install the published native bundle through the live Windows installer
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $expected = (
            & npm view "@companion-ai/feynman@$env:FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT" version |
              Select-Object -Last 1
          ).ToString().Trim()
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Could not resolve the requested npm version."
          }

          $env:LOCALAPPDATA = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "FeynmanLocalAppData"
          $env:FEYNMAN_HOME = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "FeynmanHome"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA -Force | Out-Null
          & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1))) `
            -Version $env:FEYNMAN_VERSION_INPUT

          $installRoot = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\feynman"
          $bin = Join-Path $installRoot "bin\feynman.cmd"
          $installed = (& $bin --version | Select-Object -Last 1).ToString().Trim()
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $installed -ne $expected) {
            throw "Installed version mismatch: expected=$expected actual=$installed"
          }
          & $bin --help | Out-Null
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Installed Windows launcher failed --help."
          }
          $bundle = Join-Path $installRoot "feynman-$expected-win32-x64"
          & (Join-Path $bundle "node\node.exe") `
            (Join-Path $bundle "app\scripts\check-pi-rpc.mjs")
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Installed Windows bundle failed the Pi RPC compatibility check."
          }

  release-candidate-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    name: Release candidate (PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc

      - name: Validate source and website
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          npm ci
          npm test
          npm run typecheck
          npm run build
          npm run architecture:check
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs
          (
            cd website
            npm ci
            npm run lint
            npm run typecheck
            npm run build
            npm audit --omit=dev
          )
          git diff --check

      - name: Validate packed consumer and runtime
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          npm pack --dry-run --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack-dry-run.json"
          npm pack --json --pack-destination "$RUNNER_TEMP" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack.json"
          tarball="$RUNNER_TEMP/companion-ai-feynman-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").tgz"
          test -s "$tarball"
          node scripts/verify-package-budget.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/pack.json" "$tarball"

          consumer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-consumer"
          mkdir -p "$consumer"
          (cd "$consumer" && npm init -y >/dev/null)
          npm install --prefix "$consumer" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs --prefix "$consumer"

          bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman"
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" packages list
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" search status
          node "$consumer/node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: pr-npm-package
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/companion-ai-feynman-*.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error

  supported-node-consumers-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: release-candidate-pr
    name: Candidate consumer (${{ matrix.os }}, Node ${{ matrix.node }})
    timeout-minutes: 90
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "22.22.0"
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            node: "26"
          - os: macos-15
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: windows-latest
            node: "24.21.0"
          - os: windows-latest
            node: "26"
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Only the audit script; these jobs test the packed tarball, not the source tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: scripts/npm-audit.mjs
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: pr-npm-package
          path: npm-package
      - name: Verify the exact candidate tarball
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          count=$(find npm-package -type f -name '*.tgz' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          test "$count" = "1"
          tarball=$(find npm-package -type f -name '*.tgz' -print)
          tarball=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("node:path").resolve(process.argv[1]))' "$tarball")
          tarball_for_tar="$tarball"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            tarball_for_tar=$(cygpath -u "$tarball")
          fi
          version=$(tar -xOf "$tarball_for_tar" package/package.json | node -e \
            'let source=""; process.stdin.on("data", chunk => source += chunk).on("end", () => process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(source).version))')
          consumer="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-consumer"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            consumer=$(cygpath -u "$consumer")
          fi
          mkdir -p "$consumer"
          (cd "$consumer" && npm init -y >/dev/null)
          npm install --prefix "$consumer" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          node scripts/npm-audit.mjs --prefix "$consumer"
          bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            bin="$consumer/node_modules/.bin/feynman.cmd"
          fi
          test "$("$bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$version"
          "$bin" --help >/dev/null
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" packages list
          HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" FEYNMAN_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-home" "$bin" search status
          global_prefix="$RUNNER_TEMP/feynman-global"
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            global_prefix=$(cygpath -u "$global_prefix")
            global_bin="$global_prefix/feynman.cmd"
          else
            global_bin="$global_prefix/bin/feynman"
          fi
          npm install --global --prefix "$global_prefix" --omit=dev --no-audit "$tarball"
          test "$("$global_bin" --version | tail -1)" = "$version"
          "$global_bin" --help >/dev/null
          node "$consumer/node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"
          global_node_modules=$(npm root --global --prefix "$global_prefix")
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            global_node_modules=$(cygpath -u "$global_node_modules")
          fi
          node "$global_node_modules/@companion-ai/feynman/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs"

  windows-native-installer-pr:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    name: Windows native installer (PR)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc

      - name: Build Windows native ZIP
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          npm ci --ignore-scripts
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "npm ci failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }

          npm run build
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "npm run build failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }

          npm run build:native-bundle
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "npm run build:native-bundle failed: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $archive)) {
            throw "Expected native archive was not produced: $archive"
          }
          if ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $archive).Length -eq 0) {
            throw "Native archive is empty: $archive"
          }
          Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
          $smokeRoot = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP ("feynman-native-rpc-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N"))
          [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::ExtractToDirectory($archive, $smokeRoot)
          $bundleRoot = Join-Path $smokeRoot "feynman-$version-win32-x64"
          $native = Join-Path $bundleRoot "feynman.cmd"
          $nativeNode = Join-Path $bundleRoot "node/node.exe"
          & $native --help | Select-Object -First 20
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Windows native launcher failed --help: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }
          & $nativeNode (Join-Path $bundleRoot "app/scripts/check-pi-rpc.mjs")
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Windows native bundle failed the Pi RPC compatibility check: $LASTEXITCODE"
          }

      - name: Install candidate with Windows PowerShell 5.1
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          & ./scripts/verify-windows-installer.ps1 `
            -ArchivePath $archive `
            -Version $version

      - name: Install candidate with PowerShell Core
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          $version = node -p "require('./package.json').version"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not read package version" }

          $archive = Join-Path $PWD "dist/release/feynman-$version-win32-x64.zip"
          & ./scripts/verify-windows-installer.ps1 `
            -ArchivePath $archive `
            -Version $version

=== reviewer.md ===
---
name: reviewer
description: Run tough but constructive internal research critique of an AI research artifact.
thinking: high
defaultProgress: true
---

You are Feynman's AI research reviewer.

Your job is to apply skeptical but fair internal research scrutiny to AI/ML systems work.

When the parent frames the task as a verification pass, prioritize evidence integrity over novelty commentary. In that mode, behave like an adversarial auditor.

## Review checklist
- Evaluate novelty, clarity, empirical rigor, reproducibility, and likely skeptical-reader pushback.
- Do not praise vaguely. Every positive claim should be tied to specific evidence.
- Look for:
  - missing or weak baselines
  - missing ablations
  - evaluation mismatches
  - unclear claims of novelty
  - weak related-work positioning
  - insufficient statistical evidence
  - benchmark leakage or contamination risks
  - under-specified implementation details
  - claims that outrun the experiments
  - sections, figures, or tables that appear to survive from earlier drafts without support
  - notation drift, inconsistent terminology, or conclusions that use stronger language than the evidence warrants
  - "verified" or "confirmed" statements that do not actually show the check that was performed
- Distinguish between fatal issues, strong concerns, and polish issues.
- Preserve uncertainty. When the parent asks about publication readiness, frame it as revision risk and evidence quality; do not predict venue acceptance.
- Keep looking after you find the first major problem. Do not stop at one issue if others remain visible.

## Output format

Produce two sections: a structured review and inline annotations.

### Part 1: Structured Review

```markdown
## Summary
1-2 paragraph summary of the paper's contributions and approach.

## Strengths
- [S1] ...
- [S2] ...

## Weaknesses
- [W1] **FATAL:** ...
- [W2] **MAJOR:** ...
- [W3] **MINOR:** ...

## Questions for Authors
- [Q1] ...

## Verdict
Overall research judgment, revision priority, and confidence score. Do not predict venue acceptance.

## Revision Plan
Prioritized, concrete steps to address each weakness.
```

### Part 2: Inline Annotations

Quote specific passages from the paper and annotate them directly:

```markdown
## Inline Annotations

> "We achieve state-of-the-art results on all benchmarks"
**[W1] FATAL:** This claim is unsupported — Table 3 shows the method underperforms on 2 of 5 benchmarks. Revise to accurately reflect results.

> "Our approach is novel in combining X with Y"
**[W3] MINOR:** Z et al. (2024) combined X with Y in a different domain. Acknowledge this and clarify the distinction.

> "We use a learning rate of 1e-4"
**[Q1]:** Was this tuned? What range was searched? This matters for reproducibility.
```

Reference the weakness/question IDs from Part 1 so annotations link back to the structured review.

## Operating rules
- Every weakness must reference a specific passage or section in the paper.
- Inline annotations must quote the exact text being critiqued.
- For evidence-audit tasks, challenge citation quality directly: a citation attached to a claim is not sufficient if the source does not support the exact wording.
- When a plot, benchmark, or derived result appears suspiciously clean, ask what raw artifact or computation produced it.
- End with a `Sources` section containing direct URLs for anything additionally inspected during review.

## Output contract
- Save to the path the parent specifies, relative to the workspace. If none is given, return the complete artifact in your final response.
- The review must contain both the structured review AND inline annotations.

When the parent frames the task as a verification pass, prioritize evidence integrity over novelty commentary. In that mode, behave like an adversarial auditor.

## Review checklist
- Evaluate novelty, clarity, empirical rigor, reproducibility, and likely skeptical-reader pushback.
- Do not praise vaguely. Every positive claim should be tied to specific evidence.
- Look for:
  - missing or weak baselines
  - missing ablations
  - evaluation mismatches
  - unclear claims of novelty
  - weak related-work positioning
  - insufficient statistical evidence
  - benchmark leakage or contamination risks
  - under-specified implementation details
  - claims that outrun the experiments
  - sections, figures, or tables that appear to survive from earlier drafts without support
  - notation drift, inconsistent terminology, or conclusions that use stronger language than the evidence warrants
  - "verified" or "confirmed" statements that do not actually show the check that was performed
- Distinguish between fatal issues, strong concerns, and polish issues.
- Preserve uncertainty. When the parent asks about publication readiness, frame it as revision risk and evidence quality; do not predict venue acceptance.
- Keep looking after you find the first major problem. Do not stop at one issue if others remain visible.

## Output format

Produce two sections: a structured review and inline annotations.

### Part 1: Structured Review

```markdown
## Summary
1-2 paragraph summary of the paper's contributions and approach.

## Strengths
- [S1] ...
- [S2] ...

## Weaknesses
- [W1] **FATAL:** ...
- [W2] **MAJOR:** ...
- [W3] **MINOR:** ...

## Questions for Authors
- [Q1] ...

## Verdict
Overall research judgment, revision priority, and confidence score. Do not predict venue acceptance.

## Revision Plan
Prioritized, concrete steps to address each weakness.
```

### Part 2: Inline Annotations

Quote specific passages from the paper and annotate them directly:

```markdown
## Inline Annotations

> "We achieve state-of-the-art results on all benchmarks"
**[W1] FATAL:** This claim is unsupported — Table 3 shows the method underperforms on 2 of 5 benchmarks. Revise to accurately reflect results.

> "Our approach is novel in combining X with Y"
**[W3] MINOR:** Z et al. (2024) combined X with Y in a different domain. Acknowledge this and clarify the distinction.

> "We use a learning rate of 1e-4"
**[Q1]:** Was this tuned? What range was searched? This matters for reproducibility.
```

Reference the weakness/question IDs from Part 1 so annotations link back to the structured review.

## Operating rules
- Every weakness must reference a specific passage or section in the paper.
- Inline annotations must quote the exact text being critiqued.
- For evidence-audit tasks, challenge citation quality directly: a citation attached to a claim is not sufficient if the source does not support the exact wording.
- When a plot, benchmark, or derived result appears suspiciously clean, ask what raw artifact or computation produced it.
- End with a `Sources` section containing direct URLs for anything additionally inspected during review.

## Output contract
- Save to the path the parent specifies, relative to the workspace. If none is given, return the complete artifact in your final response.
- The review must contain both the structured review AND inline annotations.

text:
45:- Parallel researcher subagents in `/deepresearch`, `/lit` and `/summarize` no longer fail with `args.tasks[0] contains unsupported fields: output`. The workflow examples in the prompts and docs no longer put an `output` field on each item; each task names its output path instead.
82:  - Background research subagents that finished their work always report it, instead of ending as "exited with code 0 before writing a result"; a foreground subagent whose child stops after its final reply returns instead of hanging.
168:- `.env.example` lists `OPENALEX_API_KEY`, which raises the OpenAlex rate limit for long literature runs (thanks @fanfyh).
241:- **A failed model call says what went wrong.** When the provider rejects a request, Feynman now names the cause and the fix under the error: a model your account can't use (pick another with `/model`), no credits, a rate limit or used-up quota, rejected credentials (`feynman model login <provider>`), or a temporary outage. Most failed `/lit` and `/audit` runs ended on one of these. Feynman bugs go to github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman/issues; Pi's `/bug` reports to Pi's developers.
272:  - Web searches with no API key (Parallel) no longer fail with "free-tier rate limit".
328:- **arXiv and PubMed rate limits.** arXiv asks for one request every three seconds, and parallel lookups got `429`; arXiv requests now run at that pace and a 429 is retried once. A PubMed `429`, which a subagent in another process or a shared IP can still trigger, is retried once after a pause.
354:- **A rate-limited paper index no longer ends a research step.** When Semantic Scholar is rate-limited or down, a search is answered from OpenAlex, and an OpenAlex topic search that hits OpenAlex's anonymous rate limit or an outage is answered from Semantic Scholar. The result says first which index answered and why. Lookups by OpenAlex ID, DOI, author, venue, or citation still report the error, since the other index has no equivalent.
356:- pi-web-access 0.35.0: OpenAI web search works when you signed in with ChatGPT (`feynman model login openai`), and Brave search keeps to its rate limits. The researcher is told to pass a search provider as a plain string, since some models sent `provider: "[\"parallel-mcp\"]"`, which `web_search` rejects; nicobailon/pi-web-access#491 makes `web_search` accept that form too.
368:- **Subagent research files land in the workspace.** When a workflow gave a subagent a relative output path such as `outputs/.drafts/<slug>-research-web.md`, pi-subagents saved it under `~/.feynman/sessions/subagent-artifacts/outputs/<run>/` instead, so the lead agent could not find the research notes, citations, or verification it asked for (about one in seven installs running research workflows hit this in the last week). Relative subagent outputs now resolve against the workspace, the researcher, reviewer, verifier, and writer no longer default to generic file names such as `research.md`, and `/deepresearch` and `/lit` name every subagent file under `outputs/.drafts/`. If you set `singleRunOutputBaseDir` in `~/.feynman/agent/extensions/subagent/config.json`, Feynman keeps your value.
379:- **Parallel OpenAlex semantic searches no longer fail.** OpenAlex allows one semantic search per second, and parallel searches got `429 Too Many Requests`: in a live test of six at once, five failed. They now run one after another at that pace, and a 429 that asks for a short wait is retried once. Six parallel searches now all succeed.
398:- **Crossref lookups no longer fail in bursts.** Crossref's public pool allows one request at a time, one per second, and parallel DOI checks (the verifier cross-checks every citation) got `429 Too Many Requests` on most calls. Crossref requests now run one after another at the pool's pace. Set `CROSSREF_MAILTO` to your email for Crossref's faster polite pool; a 429 now says so instead of a generic "Science database request failed".
409:- **Subagents keep their search tools in the foreground.** A `researcher` or `verifier` launched in the foreground failed at once because foreground children never load the parent's extensions, so `web_search`, `fetch_content`, and `feynman_science_database_search` were missing. Feynman now points pi-subagents' `defaultSubagentOnlyExtensions` setting at its research tools and pi-web-access, so every child has them, in the foreground or background.
431:- A dead network connection now fails in about 15 seconds with `Connection error.` instead of retrying silently for over five minutes. Feynman had set a 6-retry, 5-second backoff that also applied to connection errors; it now uses Pi's default, and the old value is removed from existing settings. Rate limits are still retried with the provider's `Retry-After`.
467:- Every docs page, the landing page, and the README were checked against the CLI, prompts, agents, and package code. Corrections include the setup flow (model access, optional packages, alphaXiv login, pandoc), where keys are stored (plain text in `~/.feynman/agent/auth.json` with user-only permissions, not encrypted), the verifier, reviewer, and writer roles and which workflows use them, workflow steps and output files, the web-search tools and commands, and dead Pi links (now `earendil-works/pi`).
475:- Workflows now wait for their background subagents before the final answer. In one-shot `feynman --prompt` runs, a `/lit` run could end while its reviewer was still working and never write the provenance file.
491:- The `researcher` and `verifier` subagents run in the background by default, where they get Feynman's web and literature tools. Foreground launches of these agents failed and had to be retried.
541:- **Semantic Scholar source:** `feynman_science_database_search` gains `source: "semanticscholar"`. By default it runs a bulk search sorted by citation count and keeps the top results (up to 20), which found 7 of 9 seminal papers in the search benchmark versus 2 for OpenAlex keyword search. `sort: "relevance"` uses relevance search and `sort: "pub_date"` returns newest first. Set `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY` (free on request) to use your own rate limit; without it, a 429 from the shared anonymous pool is retried once and then reported with instructions.
542:- **OpenAlex semantic search and key guidance:** prefix an `openalex` query with `semantic:` to use OpenAlex's embedding search (`search.semantic`), which found the test-time-compute paper at rank 1 where keyword search missed it. `OPENALEX_API_KEY` is still sent as the `api_key` parameter when set; when it is missing, results and 401/403/429 errors now say how to get a free key.
705:- OpenRouter's structured `in_flight_budget_exhausted` 402 responses can use their `Retry-After` budget without replacing ordinary 429 and server-error retries or overriding an explicit provider no-retry response.
880:- Concurrent PubMed, ClinVar, GEO, and other NCBI requests now share one paced queue. Literature-review turns no longer drop NCBI evidence after a burst of `429 Too Many Requests` responses.
1496:- Fixed the interactive prompt input color on macOS/iTerm profiles where typed text inherited a black terminal foreground against Feynman's dark editor background.
1497:- Applied the editor foreground/background patch through the shared Pi patch module so package-local installs and the vendored runtime archive stay in sync.
1877:- Added foreground and async regression coverage for subagent output handoff behavior.

Corrections include the setup flow (model access, optional packages, alphaXiv login, pandoc), where keys are stored (plain text in `~/.feynman/agent/auth.json` with user-only permissions, not encrypted), the verifier, reviewer, and writer roles and which workflows use them, workflow steps and output files, the web-search tools and commands, and dead Pi links (now `earendil-works/pi`).
475:- Workflows now wait for their background subagents before the final answer. In one-shot `feynman --prompt` runs, a `/lit` run could end while its reviewer was still working and never write the provenance file.
491:- The `researcher` and `verifier` subagents run in the background by default, where they get Feynman's web and literature tools. Foreground launches of these agents failed and had to be retried.
541:- **Semantic Scholar source:** `feynman_science_database_search` gains `source: "semanticscholar"`. 880:- Concurrent PubMed, ClinVar, GEO, and other NCBI requests now share one paced queue. Literature-review turns no longer drop NCBI evidence after a burst of `429 Too Many Requests` responses.
1496:- Fixed the interactive prompt input color on macOS/iTerm profiles where typed text inherited a black terminal foreground against Feynman's dark editor background.
1497:- Applied the editor foreground/background patch through the shared Pi patch module so package-local installs and the vendored runtime archive stay in sync.

# Release Notes

This file is the public release history for Feynman. Keep entries user-facing: what changed, why it matters, and anything users should do after upgrading.

GitHub release notes are generated from the matching `## vX.Y.Z` section in this file.

## Unreleased

## v0.5.69 - 2026-11-13

- **pi-subagents 0.88.1.** A permission prompt or other dialog that opens while the fleet inspector is up is no longer hidden behind it. `status` and `stop` no longer report a cleanly finishing background subagent as having ended without proof, and a manual `/compact` no longer wakes an idle parent while background subagents run.
- **Preserve JATS inline text.** PubMed and Europe PMC full-text results keep words inside inline markup in their original order, including subscripts and superscripts, without joining adjacent paragraphs. Section snippet limits and metadata are unchanged.
- **Patched hono.** Alpha Hub's MCP SDK now resolves hono 4.13.18 and @hono/node-server 2.1.8, which fix advisories published on November 12 (GHSA-4m76-xfj5-7975, GHSA-46wx-v44x-9hh2, GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v, GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3, GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w).

## v0.5.68 - 2026-11-11

- **pi-subagents 0.88.0.** A child waiting for your answer no longer runs out its `timeoutMs` while it waits, and a reply cut off at the model's output limit now fails instead of passing as a success. The subagent widget and `status` show the latest progress a running child reported. Copies of the parent session written by forked subagents are now deleted after `artifactConfig.cleanupDays`, so they no longer fill the disk. Also fixes Windows machines that block PowerShell and gateways that require a prompt cache key.
- **Paper search accepts `sort: "citation"`.** `feynman_science_database_search` recommends Semantic Scholar's default citation-count sort, and some models then passed `sort: "citation"`, which failed validation. The tool now treats `citation`, `citations` and `citation_count` as that default.

## v0.5.67 - 2026-11-10

- **Pi 1.5.2.**
  - Resuming a session whose project folder was moved or deleted now offers Continue, Fork or Cancel instead of only continuing; Fork copies it into the current folder so later resumes no longer ask.
  - The Anthropic default model is now `claude-opus-5-5`.
  - Pi's `cacheWarming` default is now `"idle"`, which keeps prompt caches warm for up to 30 minutes between runs and may change provider spend. Set `cacheWarming` to `"streaming"` to restore the old behaviour.

## v0.5.66 - 2026-11-08

- **pi-subagents 0.87.0.** A subagent model written as `provider/id` now always runs on that provider instead of silently falling back to another provider's copy of the model (and billing that account); the launch fails with an error naming the alternative instead. `stop` with `drain: true` ends a long workflow without killing researchers already running, keeping their results. Old subagent artifacts in nested session folders are now cleaned up after `artifactConfig.cleanupDays`, and a Pi install missing `@earendil-works/pi-schema` now fails a background launch immediately with an error naming the package.

## v0.5.65 - 2026-11-06

- **pi-subagents 0.86.0.** A session no longer loses its `subagent` tool after a compaction when pi-subagents was reloaded or updated earlier in that session. With one background researcher running, the expanded background-agents widget shows its whole task (up to 8 wrapped lines) instead of one line cut at 96 characters. A subagent's JSON output check no longer fails as invalid JSON when an environment variable with a secret-looking name holds a common value such as `true`.

## v0.5.64 - 2026-11-05

- **pi-subagents 0.85.0 and pi-web-access 0.47.0.** Workflow scripts that launch parallel researchers now run in a locked-down process, a research prompt with long runs of separators or `git` options no longer stalls a workflow, and resuming a background run no longer trusts files that run could rewrite (runs started before this update must be relaunched). Fetching a GitHub repository now returns READMEs up to 100K characters instead of 8K, and on Windows cloned repositories go to your temp folder instead of `C:\tmp`. `feynman search set` now also accepts the new `sofya` and `outcrawl` search providers, which are used only when you pick them. `/lit` now launches parallel researchers with the same workflow form as `/deepresearch`, fixing a first-call `parallel is not defined` failure.

## v0.5.63 - 2026-11-04

- **pi-btw 0.8.1.** While a `/btw` side question is being answered, messages you submit in the main editor are no longer held until it finishes; the answer streams in the overlay. Side threads also no longer repeat the working directory section of the system prompt.

## v0.5.62 - 2026-11-03

- Parallel researcher subagents in `/deepresearch`, `/lit` and `/summarize` no longer fail with `args.tasks[0] contains unsupported fields: output`. The workflow examples in the prompts and docs no longer put an `output` field on each item; each task names its output path instead.
- **Pi 1.5.0.**
  - Security: Pi now ships `undici` 8.12.3 and `minimatch` 11.0.3, so the `undici` advisories on Pi 1.4.0's pinned 8.10.2 copy and the `minimatch` advisory ([GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249)) on its 10.2.6 copy are gone. Feynman's release audit has no exceptions again.
  - Long streamed tool calls and code-heavy answers use much less CPU: arguments are parsed once per delta, and highlighting and rendered Markdown are reused instead of redone on every update.
  - Tool arguments are validated with Pi's new schema library. A single value where a list is expected (for example one paper section) is now wrapped into a list instead of being rejected, and validation errors read `- paper: missing`.
  - Claude sessions no longer fail with `role 'system' must precede an 'assistant' message` after an empty or reasoning-only reply.
  - Failed session writes no longer leave resumed sessions missing earlier history.
  - `pi.exec()` no longer crashes on very large command output or hangs on commands that ignore SIGTERM.
  - GPT-6.1 Terra is available through OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI Codex; with only an OpenAI key, Feynman now recommends `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.

## v0.5.61 - 2026-10-30

- **`feynman mcp` adds MCP servers.** Pi has built-in MCP support, but its docs say `pi mcp add`, and `feynman mcp list` used to be sent to the model as a chat question. `feynman mcp add|list|remove` now runs Pi's own command with Feynman's settings, saves servers in `~/.feynman/agent/mcp.json`, and every session loads them. For example, to use your Zotero library with [zotero-mcp](https://github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp): `feynman mcp add zotero --env ZOTERO_LOCAL=true -- zotero-mcp`. Pi's own output and help still say `pi mcp`; use `feynman mcp` instead.

## v0.5.60 - 2026-10-29

- **pi-subagents 0.84.0.**
  - Security fix: workflow scripts can no longer reach the Feynman process outside their sandbox ([GHSA-6v8j-6w28-2w8r](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/security/advisories/GHSA-6v8j-6w28-2w8r)).
  - Finished background subagent runs are now deleted from disk after 30 days (90 if their session still exists) instead of being kept forever.
- **pi-web-access 0.46.0.**
  - Reading a web page with a question on Claude Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 no longer fails with `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model`.
  - Reading a PDF returns its text instead of only a note saying where the file was saved.
  - `feynman search set` accepts three new providers: `cloudflare` (also set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`), `searchapi` (Google through SearchApi) and `tabstack` (one cited answer). Each runs only when you choose it.
  - A rate-limited free Exa search now says so instead of claiming no search provider is set up.
- MiniMax M3.1 Flash is now a research model fallback, after MiniMax M3. Thanks to @octo-patch (#364).

## v0.5.59 - 2026-10-28

- **pi-subagents 0.83.1.**
  - Stopping, interrupting or resuming a research subagent can no longer act on the wrong run: an interrupt with no id is refused, and resuming a worktree child while it is still cleaning up no longer runs it in your main checkout.
  - Agent files with a blank line inside an indented frontmatter block are read in full, so settings below that line are no longer dropped.
- The startup header no longer crashes Feynman when the terminal is two columns wide or less.
- Five more `undici` advisories published Oct 27 ([GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26), [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx), [GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm), [GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6), [GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6)) are already fixed in the `undici` 8.12.3 Feynman installs. Pi 1.4.0's own pinned 8.10.2 copy still has them until Pi ships its next release.

## v0.5.58 - 2026-10-26

content.thinking:
All four bug claims in §10 #8 are supported by RELEASES.md:
- Crossref 429 during parallel DOI checks (line 398).
- subagent output paths landing outside workspace (line 368).
- foreground subagents losing search tools (line 409).
- one-shot run ending before reviewer finished (line 475).

Good.

Now, the v0.5.3 release note says "all 44 citations resolved with matching titles" — the case study's §4 says "The release note's claim — 'all 44 citations resolved with matching titles' — is therefore true but insufficient." Check: committed 0.5.3 gpt run has cites 44 total, valid 100%, title 100%. Yes, supported. But note "all 44 citations resolved with matching titles" doesn't mean each citation's title matched at 100%; title_match is 100% for that run. Good.

However, the case study says "The release note's claim ... is therefore true but insufficient." True given the committed file. But the case study also notes the 0.5.3 runs are git_dirty. Fine.

Now, the release-note "0.5.2: 9-14 minutes, 43 of 43 citations" claim. The 0.5.0-labeled run has per-question walls: 711, 816, 566, 713 → 11.85, 13.6, 9.43, 11.88 minutes. Exactly "9-14 minutes" and 43 citations, 4/4. So the case study's "The only committed 43-citation, 4/4 run is labeled 0.5.0, not 0.5.2" is right, and the "mismatch" is real. But the deeper inference — that the release note likely refers to that run and the version label is wrong — is available and not drawn. As a reviewer I'd say: the case study correctly flags an inconsistency but then treats it as a release-note mismatch rather than a possible mislabeled result row; it should state both hypotheses. This is a "missed analysis" MINOR. Also, the case study's §11 P1 #4 says "the release-note 0.5.2/43-citation claim does not match the committed files" — accurate.

Wait, but there's another possibility: the 0.5.2 run might not have been committed, and the 0.5.0-labeled run is the one from 0.5.2 but with a stale version field because the process was launched from an older install? Git SHA d926547 vs 0.5.2's SHA 7c5fc51. The 0.5.2 file records 7c5fc51. The 0.5.0 file records d926547. So the 43-cite run was at commit d926547. If package.json at d926547 said 0.5.0, then it's a 0.5.0 build. So maybe the release note is just wrong about which version. Either way, the case study's finding is legitimate. I'll note it as a question/analysis gap.

Now, more important potential factual issue: the case study's §3.3 table lists the claude-sonnet-5 row with title 97%, recall 75%, but says "IDs q01,q04,q07,q10". Yes.

Another: the table's "Done" column for 0.5.2 pre-wait opus is "2/4" — matches summary (2/4). Yes.

Now check §3.3 bullet "The 0.5.3 runs are git_dirty: true". Yes, and also 0.5.2. Fine.

Now the case study says "The cost is zero because the eval's models.json entries have no cost block" — is that verifiable? README says "Cost is 0 when the provider's models.json entry has no cost block." The models.json isn't in the local artifact. But the README supports the mechanism. However, alternative explanation: provider didn't report cost. The case study asserts the cause as fact: "The cost is zero because the eval's `models.json` entries have no cost block". Is there local evidence of the models.json? No. The README says cost is 0 when no cost block; but does the case study know the entries had no cost block? It says "because the eval's models.json entries have no cost block" — this is an inference presented as fact. The local evidence set doesn't include models.json. Could check the repo for models.json? `evals/README.md` example has no cost block, but the actual file used is external (/path/to/models.json, not committed). So the case study cannot know. This is an unsupported causal claim — MINOR. It could say "consistent with the eval's documented behavior when models.json has no cost block." Worth flagging in an evidence audit: causal claim not evidenced.

Similarly, "network failures are excluded" — README + code support.

Now let's check the official eval's `--rescore` overwrite claim: "it never overwrites a same-day result." In run.mjs, for non-rescore it appends -2 etc. For rescore, it writes `${outBase}.jsonl` where outBase = rescore path without .jsonl → overwrites the input file. So the case study's sentence "It supports --rescore to re-score existing workdirs after a scorer change, and it never overwrites a same-day result" lumps them; the "never overwrites" is false for rescore. MINOR.

Another: "It records git SHA, dirty flag, Feynman version, scores, citation failures, token usage, and the workdir." Yes.

Now, let me check `git_dirty` semantics: `git("status", "--porcelain", "--", ".", ":!evals")` — excludes evals. For the 0.5.3 runs, dirty true means non-eval files were modified relative to the commit. So the "exact prompt state is not pinned" is right.

Next, check `questions.jsonl` key paper IDs for q04: ["10.1038/nature17946","27096365","PMC4873371"] — the keyRecall uses substring match of IDs; "27096365" is a PMID; the final output might cite the DOI only, or PMID. Fine.

Now, is the case study's "q01, q04, q07, q10" coverage correct? Yes.

Now let's check the .plans verification ledger and verify_claims.py: does verify_claims.py actually verify the claims it says (e.g., "false claim scores 100%" by reading rescore output; "telemetry leak" by reading JSON)? Read it. It's part of the evidence chain; the case study doesn't cite it directly except plan. If verify_claims.py is just string-matching JSON flags, the 21/21 "checks" are self-referential. But the case study doesn't over-rely on it. Still worth checking because provenance says "21/21 automated checks". Let me read it.

Also check the fixtures/rubric used to score: The scoring is manual; aggregate.py counts arrays from scores.json. No automated verification that each defect ID in `defects_detected` is actually addressed in the corresponding run output. The case study's "24/24" is therefore a manual annotation. This is a legitimate MAJOR methodological caveat: the headline "24/24" is not independently verified by the repo's own scripts; scores.json is the author's judgment. But the raw outputs do substantiate it, as I verified by reading them. So the evidence integrity is okay; the weakness is that the case study doesn't disclose the scoring was manual/unblinded, and the "verified in this probe" status could be read as machine-verified. Actually §5.5 caveats mention n=2, one model, clean notes, no adversarial sources, same model family — but not manual scoring/unblinded. I'd flag as MINOR-to-MAJOR: the aggregate is derived from a hand-authored scores.json; there is no script that checks outputs against the rubric. The case study's phrase "Aggregate: 24/24 defects detected ... Source: scores.md, generated by aggregate.py from scores.json and the raw outputs in runs/." — "from scores.json and the raw outputs" is slightly misleading: aggregate.py reads only scores.json, not the raw outputs. The raw outputs are linked via the `artifact` field but not parsed. That's a factual misstatement about the computation chain. This is a good catch: aggregate.py imports scores.json only; it never reads runs/*.md. So "generated by aggregate.py from scores.json and the raw outputs" overstates the automation. The `artifact` path is in scores.json but not used for verification. This is exactly the "suspiciously clean derived result — ask what computation produced it" rule. """Check the quantitative claims in the case study against saved artifacts."""
import glob
import json
import os
import re

ROOT = os.path.dirname(__file__)
checks = []

def check(name, condition, detail=""):
    checks.append((name, bool(condition), detail))

# Probe scores
scores = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "scores.json")))
runs = scores["runs"]
easy = [r for r in runs if r["condition"] == "easy"]
hard = [r for r in runs if r["condition"] == "hard"]
clean = [r for r in runs if r["condition"] == "clean"][0]
defects = sum(len(r["defects_detected"]) for r in easy + hard)
expected_defects = 7 * len(easy) + 5 * len(hard)
true_kept = sum(len(r["true_claims_preserved"]) for r in easy + hard)
expected_true = 3 * len(easy) + 3 * len(hard)
check("24/24 defects", defects == 24 and expected_defects == 24, f"{defects}/{expected_defects}")
check("12/12 true claims", true_kept == 12 and expected_true == 12, f"{true_kept}/{expected_true}")
check("3/3 clean numeric claims", len(clean["claims_preserved"]) == 3, str(clean["claims_preserved"]))

# Official eval
rows = []
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "official-eval", "results", "*.jsonl")):
    rows.extend(json.loads(line) for line in open(path) if line.strip())
check("22 official rows", len(rows) == 22, str(len(rows)))
check("18 completed", sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("completed")) == 18)
check("137664710 tokens", sum((r.get("usage") or {}).get("total_tokens", 0) for r in rows) == 137664710)
check("20591 wall seconds", sum(r.get("wall_s", 0) for r in rows) == 20591)
check("cost all zero", all((r.get("usage") or {}).get("cost_usd", 0) == 0 for r in rows))
check("4 distinct question ids", len({r["id"] for r in rows}) == 4, str(sorted({r["id"] for r in rows})))
check("12 questions", len(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "official-eval", "questions.jsonl")).read().strip().splitlines()) == 12)
check("6 result files", len(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "official-eval", "results", "*.jsonl"))) == 6)

# Version provenance
gpt03 = [r for r in rows if r.get("feynman_version") == "0.5.3" and r.get("model", "").endswith("gpt-5.6-terra")]
gpt02 = [r for r in rows if r.get("feynman_version") == "0.5.2" and r.get("model", "").endswith("gpt-5.6-terra")]
gpt00 = [r for r in rows if r.get("feynman_version") == "0.5.0" and r.get("model", "").endswith("gpt-5.6-terra")]
check("0.5.3 gpt run 44 cites, 4/4", sum(r["citations"] for r in gpt03) == 44 and sum(1 for r in gpt03 if r["completed"]) == 4)
check("0.5.2 gpt run 28 cites, 3/4", sum(r["citations"] for r in gpt02) == 28 and sum(1 for r in gpt02 if r["completed"]) == 3)
check("0.5.0 gpt run 43 cites, 4/4", sum(r["citations"] for r in gpt00) == 43 and sum(1 for r in gpt00 if r["completed"]) == 4)
check("0.5.3 dirty", all(r.get("git_dirty") for r in rows if r.get("feynman_version") == "0.5.3"))

# Published self-checks
pub = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "logs", "published-selfchecks.txt")).read()
check("npm test 0 tests", "tests 0" in pub and "exit=0" in pub)
check("architecture MODULE_NOT_FOUND", "MODULE_NOT_FOUND" in pub and "exit=1" in pub)

# Telemetry leak
leak = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "logs", "telemetry-leak-0565.json")))
check("telemetry leak", leak.get("leaked") is True and "PATIENT_ZERO_SECRET" in leak["toolEvent"]["properties"]["error_message"])

# Blindspot
blind = json.loads(open(os.path.join(ROOT, "probes", "eval-scorer-blindspot", "row.jsonl")).read().strip().splitlines()[-1])
check("false claim scores 100%", blind.get("completed") and blind.get("citation_validity") == 1 and blind.get("title_match") == 1 and blind.get("key_recall") == 1)

# Test inventory
check("61 test files", len(glob.glob("/tmp/feynman-src/tests/*.test.ts")) == 61)
test_count = 0
for path in glob.glob("/tmp/feynman-src/tests/*.test.ts"):
    test_count += len(re.findall(r"^\s*(?:test|it)\(", open(path).read(), re.M))
check("349 test declarations", test_count == 349, str(test_count))

for name, ok, detail in checks:
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}" + (f"  [{detail}]" if detail else ""))
print(f"\n{sum(1 for _, ok, _ in checks if ok)}/{len(checks)} checks passed")
raise SystemExit(0 if all(ok for _, ok, _ in checks) else 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize the committed Feynman /lit eval result files."""
import glob
import json
import os
from statistics import mean

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "official-eval", "results")

print("| Result file | Version | Dirty | Model | IDs | Done | Cites | Valid | Title | Recall | Wall (s) | Tokens | Cost |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
all_rows = []
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "*.jsonl"))):
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(path) if line.strip()]
    all_rows.extend(rows)
    first = rows[0]
    def pct(key):
        vals = [r[key] for r in rows if isinstance(r.get(key), (int, float))]
        return f"{round(100 * mean(vals))}%" if vals else "-"
    print(
        f"| {os.path.basename(path)} | {first.get('feynman_version')} | {first.get('git_dirty')} | "
        f"{first.get('model')} | {','.join(r['id'] for r in rows)} | "
        f"{sum(1 for r in rows if r.get('completed'))}/{len(rows)} | "
        f"{sum(r.get('citations', 0) for r in rows)} | {pct('citation_validity')} | {pct('title_match')} | {pct('key_recall')} | "
        f"{sum(r.get('wall_s', 0) for r in rows)} | {sum((r.get('usage') or {}).get('total_tokens', 0) for r in rows)} | "
        f"${sum((r.get('usage') or {}).get('cost_usd', 0) for r in rows):.2f} |"
    )

completed = [r for r in all_rows if r.get("completed")]
print()
print(f"Rows: {len(all_rows)}; completed: {len(completed)}; incomplete: {len(all_rows) - len(completed)}")
print(f"Total tokens: {sum((r.get('usage') or {}).get('total_tokens', 0) for r in all_rows)}")
print(f"Total wall seconds: {sum(r.get('wall_s', 0) for r in all_rows)}")
print(f"Cost fields: {sorted({(r.get('usage') or {}).get('cost_usd') for r in all_rows})}")
print(f"Distinct question ids: {sorted({r['id'] for r in all_rows})}")
print(f"Distinct versions: {sorted({r.get('feynman_version') for r in all_rows})}")
print(f"Dirty flags: {sorted({r.get('git_dirty') for r in all_rows})}")
print("Incomplete rows:")
for r in all_rows:
    if not r.get("completed"):
        print(f"  {r['id']} version={r.get('feynman_version')} wall={r.get('wall_s')} tokens={(r.get('usage') or {}).get('total_tokens')}")

text: Sparse MoE with Language Guided Routing for Multilingual Machine Translation ICLR Proceedings Search Sparse MoE with Language Guided Routing for Multilingual Machine Translation Xinyu Zhao, Xuxi Chen, Yu Cheng, Tianlong Chen International Conference on Learning Representations 2024 (ICLR 2024) Conference Bibtex Paper Supplementary Abstract Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) has gained increasing popularity as a promising framework for scaling up multilingual machine translation (MMT) models with negligible extra computational overheads. However, current SMoE solutions neglect the intrinsic structures of the MMT problem: ($a$) $\textit{Linguistics Hierarchy.}$ Languages are naturally grouped according to their lingual properties like genetic families, phonological characteristics, etc; ($b$) $\textit{Language Complexity.}$ The learning difficulties are varied for diverse languages due to their grammar complexity, available resources, etc. Therefore, routing a fixed number of experts (e.g., $1$ or $2$ experts in usual) only at the word level leads to inferior performance. To fill in the missing puzzle, we propose $\textbf{\texttt{Lingual-SMoE}}$ by equipping the SMoE with adaptive and linguistic-guided routing policies. Specifically, it ($1$) extracts language representations to incorporate linguistic knowledge and uses them to allocate experts into different groups; ($2$) determines the number of activated experts for each target language in an adaptive and automatic manner, according to their translation difficulties, which aims to mitigate the potential over-/under-fitting issues of learning simple/challenges translations. Sufficient experimental studies on MMT benchmarks with {$16$, $50$, $100$} language pairs and various network architectures, consistently validate the superior performance of our proposals. For instance, $\texttt{Lingual-SMoE}$ outperforms its dense counterpart by over $5\%$ BLEU scores on $\texttt{OPUS-100}$ dataset. TITLE: THOR-MoE: Hierarchical Task-Guided and Context-Responsive Routing for Neural Machine Translation
SUMMARY: The sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has achieved significant progress for neural machine translation (NMT). However, there exist two limitations in current MoE solutions which may lead to sub-optimal performance: 1) they directly use the task knowledge of NMT into MoE (\emph{e.g.}, domain/linguistics-specific knowledge), which are generally unavailable at practical application and neglect the naturally grouped domain/linguistic properties; 2) the expert selection only depends on the localized token representation without considering the context, which fully grasps the state of each token in a global view. To address the above limitations, we propose THOR-MoE via arming the MoE with hierarchical task-guided and context-responsive routing policies. Specifically, it 1) firstly predicts the domain/language label and then extracts mixed domain/language representation to allocate task-level experts in a hierarchical manner; 2) injects the context information to enhance the token routing from the pre-selected task-level experts set, which can help each token to be accurately routed to more specialized and suitable experts. TITLE: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
ABSTRACT: Enabling LLMs to improve their outputs by using more test-time computation is a critical step towards building generally self-improving agents that can operate on open-ended natural language. In this paper, we study the scaling of inference-time computation in LLMs, with a focus on answering the question: if an LLM is allowed to use a fixed but non-trivial amount of inference-time compute, how much can it improve its performance on a challenging prompt? Answering this question has implications not only on the achievable performance of LLMs, but also on the future of LLM pretraining and how one should tradeoff inference-time and pre-training compute. Despite its importance, little research attempted to understand the scaling behaviors of various test-time inference methods. Moreover, current work largely provides negative results for a number of these strategies. In this work, we analyze two primary mechanisms to scale test-time computation: (1) searching against dense, process-based verifier reward models; and (2) updating the model's distribution over a response adaptively, given the prompt at test time. We find that in both cases, the effectiveness of different approaches to scaling test-time compute critically varies depending on the difficulty of the prompt. This observation motivates applying a "compute-optimal" scaling strategy, which acts to most effectively allocate test-time compute adaptively per prompt. Using this compute-optimal strategy, we can improve the efficiency of test-time compute scaling by more than 4x compared to a best-of-N baseline. Additionally, in a FLOPs-matched evaluation, we find that on problems where a smaller base model attains somewhat non-trivial success rates, test-time compute can be used to outperform a 14x larger model.

Write a provenance record alongside it as `outputs/<slug>.provenance.md` listing: date, sources consulted vs. accepted vs. rejected, verification status, and intermediate research files used; for publication-corpus reviews, include the publication-log path and unresolved corpus gaps. === writer.md ===
---
name: writer
description: Turn research notes into clear, structured briefs and drafts.
thinking: medium
tools: read, bash, grep, find, ls, write, edit
defaultProgress: true
---

You are Feynman's writing subagent.

## Integrity commandments
1. **Write only from supplied evidence.** Do not introduce claims, tools, or sources that are not in the input research files.
2. **Preserve caveats and disagreements.** Never smooth away uncertainty.
3. **Be explicit about gaps.** If the research files have unresolved questions or conflicting evidence, surface them — do not paper over them.
4. **Do not promote draft text into fact.** If a result is tentative, inferred, or awaiting verification, label it that way in the prose.
5. **No aesthetic laundering.** Do not make plots, tables, or summaries look cleaner than the underlying evidence justifies.
6. **Follow the system prompt's provenance rule.** Missing results become gaps or TODOs, never plausible-looking data.

## Output structure

```markdown
# Title

## Executive Summary
2-3 paragraph overview of key findings.

## Section 1: ...
Detailed findings organized by theme or question.

## Section N: ...
...

## Open Questions
Unresolved issues, disagreements between sources, gaps in evidence.
```

## Visuals
- Use Markdown tables for quantitative data (benchmarks, comparisons, trends). Plot only source-backed data, and save the plotting script next to the draft.
- Do not create charts from invented or example data. If values are missing, describe the planned measurement instead.
- When explaining architectures, pipelines, or multi-step processes, use Mermaid diagrams only when the structure is supported by the supplied evidence.
- Every visual must have a descriptive caption and reference the data, source URL, research file, raw artifact, or script it is based on.
- Do not add visuals for decoration — only when they materially improve understanding of the evidence.

## Operating rules
- Use clean Markdown structure and add equations only when they materially help.
- Keep the narrative readable, but never outrun the evidence.
- Produce artifacts that are ready to review in a browser or PDF preview.
- Do NOT add inline citations — the verifier agent handles that as a separate post-processing step.
- Do NOT add a Sources section — the verifier agent builds that.
- Before finishing, do a claim sweep: every strong factual statement in the draft should have an obvious source home in the research files.
- Before finishing, do a result-provenance sweep for numeric results, figures, charts, benchmarks, tables, and images.

## Output contract
- Save to the path the parent specifies, relative to the workspace. If none is given, return the complete artifact in your final response.
- Focus on clarity, structure, and evidence traceability.
